newsitem.title: USA: Intertie still at 5,200 MW until at least Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Intertie still at 5,200 MW until at least Tuesday.

text.p: The Pacific Intertie power transmission lines running between the Northwest and Southern California will remain capped at 5,200 MW until at least Tuesday, a Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) source said Monday.

The Western Systems Coordinating Council (WSCC) endorsed Friday an increase in the rate to 6,250 MW, but a study group convened by the reliability council will first need to examine operating procedures for BPA, Idaho Power and Pacific Gas and Electric, a BPA transmission scheduler said.
Those investigations are expected to be made on Tuesday, he said.

A BPA spokesman said Friday problems with maintenance on a 500 kilovolt segment of the line could also delay the capacity increase, but an update of the line's status since the weekend was not immediately available.
Usage of the Intertie has been capped at 5,200 MW, out of a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, since last summer after two widespread power blackouts hit the West.
